articles.title: PlayStation 5 Linux project upgraded to support PS5 Pro and newer firmware
articles.summary: The impressive PlayStation 5 Linux project is continuing on, and recent updates to it have again expanded what it can support. Even though one of the main people behind it quit , others seem to have taking it upon themselves to continue it on.

articles.title: Nvidia open-sources Flora to make robot video labeling 125x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra
articles.summary: Labeling one hour of robot video for 72 cents instead of $88 is what Nvidia promises with Flora, its open data engine. But the comparison with GPT-6 Astra isn't quite as lopsided as the price tag suggests.

articles.title: Hairy Armor For Combat Robot? It’s Not Terrible!
articles.summary: How well did it perform? Well enough to merit further study! Where past robots got their outer shells broken up, the hairy robot seems to have come through quite intact.

articles.title: Steam's useful Personal Calendar gets a full release
articles.summary: I forgot it was ever a Beta, because Steam's Personal Calendar is actually one of the most useful features they've added to the store recently.

articles.title: Python 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 and 3.11.18 are out
articles.summary: They address the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys . These keys are now blocked by the ssl module as a last resort against their use.

articles.title: Building a Swashplate-less Helicoper Rotor
articles.summary: [worked in theory] tested two such rotor designs: one with one hinge per rotor, and one with one hinge for both rotors. The design using a single hinge seemed less sensitive to friction, was more responsive in testing, and had a more linear control response, so he used that.

articles.title: Epic's Tim Sweeney believes AI notices on Steam are a "political statement" for the "hate mob"
articles.summary: Valve requires developers to disclose AI-generated content in games and on Steam store pages, something Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney isn't happy about. Read the full article on GamingOnLinux .

articles.title: Steam Next Fest - October 2026, here's the most-played demos so far
articles.summary: Valve sent word via email as Steam Next Fest - October 2026 beings to wind down about what has been the most popular during this event.

articles.title: Tradeoff-Aware Territory Design: A Multi-Objective Decision System for Enterprise Customer-to-Seller Allocation
articles.summary: Enterprise customer journeys are shaped not only by product experiences and marketing, but also by recurring resource-allocation decisions. In B2B go-to-market (GTM) organizations, territory carving determines which accounts receive seller coverage, which seller-account relationships are preserved, and how limited field capacity is distributed.

articles.title: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents
articles.summary: Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. However, agent effectiveness depends heavily on the surrounding harness, which typically relies on manually written skills and curated memory.

articles.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
articles.summary: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. However, unlike overt hate speech, it is often difficult to detect, even for human judges.

articles.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
articles.summary: Even a carefully proofread paper can leave small gaps in its proofs or its stated assumptions. We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version.

articles.title: Ubuntu users can now file bugs against specific Launchpad PPAs
articles.summary: With the new tracking support, users can finally problems against the packages they’ve installed from that PPA. Bugs can be about the PPA a whole, an individual source package within it or a build for a specific Ubuntu version.

articles.title: Linux 7.4 Sound Changes Merged: "The AI Flood Continues"
articles.summary: Linux sound subsystem maintainer Takashi Iwai of SUSE began the Linux 7.4 sound pull request by noting that 'the AI flood continues' with there continuing to be a lot of new patches coming as a result of AI/LLM agents devising patches as well as uncovering new kernel bugs.
